name: OpenShouter
tagline: Speak notifications, calls, and system events — privately, on your device.
pitch: OpenShouter is a FOSS Android announcer that reads notifications aloud, loops incoming caller ID until the ring stops, and speaks battery, power, and location-aware events. It combines Voice Notify-style notification TTS with classic Shouter hardware and telephony features, using only open Android APIs — no Google Play Services, Firebase, or tracking.
features: Notification reader with custom TTS format strings, per-app filters, and regex ignore/replace rules
Looping caller ID announcements that stop on answer, reject, or missed call
Battery, charger, shake-to-silence, flip-to-mute, and screen on/off mute controls
Quiet hours, headset/Bluetooth-only mode, and FOSS geofence rules (no Play Services)
Foreground service, Quick Settings tile, and home-screen master on/off widget
Local-only history via Room; MIT licensed and F-Droid-friendly
quick_start: Install Android Studio (or SDK 34+) with JDK 17; open `examples/android/`.
Follow Sprint 1 in `BUILD_PLAN.md` to scaffold the app modules (do not copy proprietary SDKs).
On a device or emulator, enable Notification Listener and required runtime permissions (`[ADB]`).
install: Requires JDK 17 and Android SDK (compile/target 35, min 26). Clone the repo, open `examples/android/`, and run `./gradlew assembleDebug` (or `gradlew.bat` on Windows). Sideload the debug APK or wait for GitHub Releases / F-Droid once Sprint 1+ ships. No Play Store In-App Updates.
usage: Work from `BUILD_PLAN.md` (🔲/✅/❌ + AGENT/HUMAN/ADB/AUTO). Type `/` in Cursor Agent chat for `/bootstrap`, `/build`, `/verify`, and `/ship`. ADRs live in `docs/adr/`. Product rules: `.cursor/rules/openshouter.mdc`. After first GitHub push, poll CI with `pwsh scripts/check-github-ci.ps1 -WaitSeconds 300`.
